gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the same false estimator claim: the half-width (a_u-a_l)/2 is used as an estimate of a, although the interval guarantee supports the midpoint (a_u+a_l)/2. Both also identify the same occurrence in Algorithm 1 and the same corrected formula.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The interval-width half-difference is not an estimator of the amplitude location; the midpoint is required to obtain the claimed epsilon accuracy and the corresponding algorithmic guarantee.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proposition and Algorithm 1 use the interval half-width as an estimator, despite only establishing that a lies in a short interval; the midpoint is the quantity whose error is bounded by epsilon.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states that the half-width is unrelated to the location of a, that the midpoint gives the claimed estimate, that Algorithm 1 repeats the faulty expression, and supplies the midpoint replacement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 concerns applying the multiplication corollary when its explicit hypotheses on register widths and m2 are not satisfied. Gold I002 concerns a different register-allocation formula in the permutation: the claimed space has a trailing m-qubit zero register although the multiplication circuit requires B qubits, so the circuit is not constructed on the claimed Hilbert space. ISSUE-005 does not recognize that specific qubit-count mismatch or the required 2A+3B+3 allocation.
